title: A tail holds on
hook: Not every tail is used in the same way.

doesNotKnow: A seahorse wraps its tail around a plant stem. What immediate effect can the hold provide?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: A seahorse wraps its tail around a plant stem. What immediate effect can the hold provide?

claims.text: A seahorse wraps its tail around a plant stem. What immediate effect can the hold provide? The second panel shows the tail curved around a stem, providing a hold. Seahorses can use their tails to grip objects and anchor themselves. The schematic depicts a possible hold, not evidence that every plant or current provides secure anchorage.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A seahorse grips a holdfast in a current. Which body part is doing the gripping? Seahorses can grip a holdfast with their tails.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/

recall.why: Seahorses can grip a holdfast with their tails.
